newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Two top Mobutu generals give selves up in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Two top Mobutu generals give selves up in Kinshasa.

text.p: The two most senior generals of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko still at large gave themselves up to Laurent Kabila's forces in Kinshasa on Wednesday in front of a crowd of jeering youths, witnesses said.

General Amela Lokima, military governor of Kinshasa and deputy armed forces chief-of-staff, and General Michel Elessi, commander of Mobutu's forces in the capital, turned up at a hotel and were taken away by security officials.
The two men, at one stage rumoured to have been killed by Mobutu loyalists angry that the armed forces were prepared to give up without a fight, were wearing civilian clothes.
Elessi was military governor of South Kivu province in eastern Zaire when it fell to Kabila's rebels, shortly after the start of the seven-month civil war.

The army's top general, Mahele Lieko Bokungo, was murdered in Kinshasa on Friday, the night before Kabila's rebels marched into the city. Diplomats say he was killed by a member or members of Mobutu's presidential guard.

Soldiers from Mobutu's army have been handing themselves in since the weekend takeover of Kinshasa. Some have re-enlisted with Kabila's forces. A presidential guard officer was summarily executed by rebel forces.
